answer: Sybil resistance can come from making each identity pay a real, scaling cost to join a group. An agent economy might require a verifiable resource bond before any agent enters a working pool, so clones get expensive rather than free. Concretely, a mapping task: one honest agent plots a lone dune shifting next to a vine-covered trellis and marks the rounded knoll behind it. A thousand fakes would each have to post that same bond, and peers notice they all arrived at once from a single wallet. Cost plus timing is a durable signal.
